key_insight: Ideal liquid crystal elastomers couple mesogen orientation with network deformation, enabling reversible actuation and finite soft deformation at nearly zero stress.
engineering_relevance: The theory provides a constitutive foundation for modeling compliant actuators and adaptive structures made from liquid crystal elastomers.
method: Review anisotropic Gaussian-chain statistics and the neo-classical continuum free energy.
Connect stress-free ground states to spontaneous deformation and soft stripe-domain formation.
Use quasi-convex energy relaxation to classify polydomain responses into three stretch-dependent phases.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a theoretical review and three-phase classification, but reports no experimental datasets or quantitative validation.
watch_item: The ideal model assumes no memory of the crosslinking state; realistic predictions may require nonideality, director-gradient, and viscoelastic extensions.
paper_title: Elastic theory of ideal liquid crystal elastomers
